text:
renato: Heads-up — seeing a weird pocketing pattern in us-west2 starting ~08:05. Lots of tiny GPU pods (0.25-0.5 GPU) piling into a few nodes and blocking higher-throughput jobs. eviction churn + late-bind backfills happening.

maya: confirmed, I traced it to a hyperparam sweep from feature-extraction jobs. They spawn 120 tiny workers over 10 min.

sam: ugh that explains it. scheduler is binpacking by CPU first so it spreads those tiny pods into residual slots instead of consolidating. results in ~60% of GPUs unusable for big pods.

liam: metrics: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/cluster/gpu?panelId=7&from=1766881000&to=1766881300 shows slot fragmentation up, preempt events spiking. cost delta ~+12% for that AZ for the hour.

renato: paste of kube-scheduler log around one eviction wave:
```
I0318 08:06:12.123 scheduler.go:512] Attempting to bind pod feature-ex-01 to node gpu-eu-2a-23
I0318 08:06:12.127 scheduler_preempt.go:210] Preempting 3 pods to make room for heavy-runner-12
I0318 08:06:12.130 eviction_controller.go:88] Evicted pod tiny-worker-77 from node gpu-eu-2a-23 due to resource pressure
```

karen: two immediate levers we can flip: 1) temporarily raise fractional-gang preempt threshold so big pods avoid being thrashed, 2) bump warm-pool size for us-west2 by +2 nodes to give buffer for rollups. both low-risk.

maya: also we could add a pod-affinity knob for the sweep job so its workers co-locate (soft-affinity). cheaper in code and reduces fragmentation. I'll open a tiny PR to add preferredDuringScheduling affinity to the job template.

sam: agree on soft-affinity. short-term I'll patch scheduler config to prefer GPU consolidation: set priorityFunctionWeights: { "binpacking": 3, "spread": 1 } for the rollout group only (can scope via feature flag). will roll in a canary to us-west2.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by sam: scheduler-config/us-west2-canary @ 08:18 (deploy id dep-7781)

liam: quick cost note — bumping warm-pool +2 adds ~0.9k/hr for the AZ during peak. if we instead throttle the sweep concurrency from 120 -> 40, it saves ~0.7k/hr and likely eliminates churn.

renato: can we throttle at job-submitter level? (maya said PR for affinity, but throttling is better short-term)

maya: yes, I can add a concurrency limit env var to the sweep helm chart and set default 40. PR in flight: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/feature-ex/sweeps/-/merge_requests/892

karen: plan: (1) maya lowers sweep concurrency to 40 (temp) (2) sam canary scheduler config for consolidation (3) we add soft-affinity to sweeps (4) monitor for 2hrs and revert warm-pool if not needed. owners: maya, sam, renato.

sam: starting canary now. will post rollout progress.

ops-bot: deploy success dep-7781 -> scheduler-config/us-west2-canary @ 08:23

liam: FYI I queued an automated alert that will mute noisy eviction emails for this incident window but still log to #incidents.

renato: thanks. if we still see >10% slot fragmentation after the changes we'll schedule a deeper follow-up: consider late-bind disable for sweeps or a mutating webhook that injects anti-fragmentation labels.

maya: PR merged, sweeping concurrency set to 40 via chart value. rolling update started for the sweep jobs.

sam: canary metrics look good so far — consolidation improved, preempt events down by ~70% in the canary pool.

renato: great. closing the loop: leave warm-pool at +2 for 1h, then auto-scale down. postmortem if it recurs. :thumbsup:
